Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=2(1-\cos\theta)$ for $0 \leq \theta \leq \pi$ (shown in blue in the picture above).
current_example.worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta)$ is given by

$$
L =  \int_{\theta_1}^{\theta_2} \sqrt{r^2 +\left(\frac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}\theta}\right)^2 }\,\textrm{d}\theta.
$$

Since $r=2(1-\cos\theta),$ we have

$$
\dfrac{\textrm{d}r}{\textrm{d}\theta} = 2\sin\theta.
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{(2-2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4-8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4{cos}^{2}⁡\theta +4{sin}^{2}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{4-8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta +4}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{8-8\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{1-\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta }\,\text{d}\theta .\end{aligned}
$$

We now use the half-angle formula $1-\cos\theta =2\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\theta}{2}\right)$ to give

$$
\begin{aligned}L & =2\sqrt{2}{\int }_{0}^{\pi }\sqrt{2{sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\sqrt{2}\cdot \sqrt{2}\cdot {\int }_{0}^{\pi }\operatorname{sin}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2})\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={-4\cdot 2(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\theta }{2}))|}_{0}^{\pi } \\  & =-8(\operatorname{cos}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-\operatorname{cos}⁡0) \\  & =-8(0-1) \\  & =8.\end{aligned}
$$
